newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains on dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains on dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed higher against the dollar on Wednesday following the decline of the U.S. currency against the mark and yen, dealers said.
"The shekel rose today following the decline of the dollar in Europe. The banks were very active today using the opportunity that the next spot is for Tuesday," said a dealer.
On Monday, Israeli Independence Day, the central bank will not set a representative rate making Tuesday the next day for setting spot rates as these are set three trading days ahead.
"The Bank of Israel had to intervene again in the market, buying more than $100 million to support the basket," said Ilan Zadka, a trader at United Mizrahi Bank.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to support the currency basket, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for three months.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4040 shekels against 3.4100 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6829 shekels against 3.6825 on Tuesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7208 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.7090 on Tuesday, and against the mark at 1.9779 shekels compared with 1.9714 on Tuesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.4020 shekels.
